gaps.quote: for the bit procedure this ring is $\mathbb F_2$, where subtraction and addition coincide
gaps.note: Wrong ring. The paper's shear (H,D) -> (H+D,D) acts on address fields over Z/q^b Z for a fixed odd prime q (Lemma matrix-shear, paper.tex lines 1395-1404; Proposition power-interchange, lines 1481-1483, uses radix-q digits). The F_2 scalars (line 689) are the data bits of the XOR network, not the address ring. With q odd, subtraction and addition do not coincide, so the three updates are not XORs and the page's F_2 example does not describe the construction.

gaps.quote: Over $\mathbb F_2$ each update is a pointwise XOR, since addition and subtraction are the same operation
gaps.note: The three updates D<-D-H, H<-H+D, D<-H-D are address permutations over Z/q^b Z with q an odd prime (paper.tex lines 1395-1404, 1425-1445, 1535-1545), not pointwise XORs of F_2 vectors. Only the gates of the network on the data bits are XORs (Proposition bit-motif-interface, line 1139). The page conflates the two.

gaps.term: linear cost of the outer updates
gaps.quote: each combining $D$ with the earlier field $H$ in linear time
gaps.note: The page gives no reason these updates take O(V) tape time when H and D are far apart with spectator fields between them. The paper gets it from Lemma ordered-affine-streams (a later field updated from earlier fields, line 556 and line 1357), which the page never states, so this reader cannot check the claim.

gaps.quote: A level-$k$ call makes $s$ calls at level $k-1$, each on volume $V/W$
gaps.note: The page never says that a width m^k field is split into m subfields of width m^(k-1) (vectors H, D of m entries), nor that each unit of rank of an edge matrix costs one interchange of such subfields. Without that construction (paper.tex lines 1495-1497, 1506-1510) the reader cannot see why the sub-calls are at level k-1.

gaps.quote: A field of $u=m^k$ bits therefore has $Q_k=O(u^\tau)$, and the interchange costs $O(Vu^\tau)$.
gaps.note: Missing hypotheses. The paper's Proposition power-interchange (lines 1476-1487) requires width exactly a power m^k and a row field before both chunks whose length is divisible by W^k. The recursion needs enough rows to split into W role streams at every level. The page omits the row condition. Arbitrary widths u need a separate lemma (Lemma chunk-swap, line 1632) with padding, not this recurrence.
